examples.title: Nested changes
examples.description: Two versions of a run's input. Added, removed and changed entries show at every depth, each led by a +, - or ~ symbol; the unchanged entries stay behind a control until asked for.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { JsonDiffViewer } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const before = {
    name: 'Nightly ETL',
    schedule: { cron: '0 2 * * *', timezone: 'UTC' },
    steps: [
      { name: 'extract', retries: 3 },
      { name: 'load', retries: 3 },
    ],
    owner: 'data-platform',
  };

  const after = {
    name: 'Nightly ETL',
    schedule: { cron: '0 3 * * *', timezone: 'UTC' },
    steps: [
      { name: 'extract', retries: 5 },
      { name: 'load', retries: 3 },
      { name: 'notify', retries: 0 },
    ],
    region: 'us-east-1',
  };
</script>

<JsonDiffViewer {before} {after} />

examples.title: A value that changes type
examples.description: Arrays compare by index, so a changed item shows at its position. A value that changes type, here a number that becomes a string, shows as one removed and one added entry rather than one change.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { JsonDiffViewer } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const before = { timeout: 30, tags: ['etl', 'nightly', 'production'] };
  const after = { timeout: '30s', tags: ['etl', 'hourly', 'production'] };
</script>

<JsonDiffViewer {before} {after} label="Run settings differences" />

examples.title: More than 200 changes in one level
examples.description: A level shows its first 200 changed entries and holds the rest behind a control that shows 200 more. Here 450 values changed, so two presses reveal them all.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { JsonDiffViewer } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const before = Object.fromEntries(
    Array.from({ length: 450 }, (_, index) => [`setting-${index}`, index]),
  );
  const after = Object.fromEntries(
    Array.from({ length: 450 }, (_, index) => [`setting-${index}`, index + 1]),
  );
</script>

<JsonDiffViewer {before} {after} label="Settings differences" />

examples.title: A comparison too large to open at once
examples.description: Nested levels add up, so the first render opens a nested level only while the whole render stays small. Here five runs each changed 150 fields: the first run opens, and the rest wait behind a "Show 150 changes" control.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { JsonDiffViewer } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const run = (offset: number) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      Array.from({ length: 150 }, (_, index) => [`field-${index}`, offset + index]),
    );

  const before = { runs: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((index) => run(index)) };
  const after = { runs: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((index) => run(index + 1000)) };
</script>

<JsonDiffViewer {before} {after} label="Run differences" />

examples.title: Identical values
examples.description: When the two values are equal the viewer says so instead of rendering an empty list.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { JsonDiffViewer } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const value = { status: 'completed', exitCode: 0 };
</script>

<JsonDiffViewer before={value} after={{ ...value }} />
